work_order.understanding: The previous plan was not wrong about the code — all five acceptance criteria passed. But its diagnosis of BUG-1 was wrong in a way that made the fix impossible, which is why QA failed with introduced_by_pr: true. v1 correctly identified the MECHANISM but made the remedy 're-word the comment' while putting rewording out of scope — a plan that cannot converge, since the comment must keep naming the spellings for AC-2's demonstration to mean anything. The new approach is DIFFERENT: declare the source boundary in src/app/globals.css instead of touching prose, verified by building both revisions and diffing the full emitted rule set. Two corrections per plan review: AC-2 no longer lists max-w-[theme(cap)] among spellings the comment names and restores the mutation demonstration; AC-6 is scoped to tests/-only spellings since .sdlc/docs-sourced rules survive by design.

review.title: The new comment at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:337 attributes QA's 548px overflow to shrink-0 on the name link, but that class produces 579px. The 548 figure comes from removing min-w-0 from the nav — a different element and a different class. The assertion itself is sound and does bite; only the stated attribution is wrong.
review.detail:
The new comment at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:337 attributes QA's 548px overflow to shrink-0 on the name link, but that class produces 579px. The 548 figure comes from removing min-w-0 from the nav — a different element and a different class. The assertion itself is sound and does bite; only the stated attribution is wrong.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:337`

Evidence: Two independent headless-Chromium sessions against `TABS_ENV=local next build && next start`, signed in through the real /sign-up form at 360x640, reproducing identically. Adding shrink-0 to the name link only (a[href="/settings"]): {"scrollW":579,"clientW":345,"nameW":344.09,"signoutRight":579.33}. Removing min-w-0 from the nav instead: {"scrollW":548,"clientW":345,"nameW":312.81,"signoutRight":548.05}. 548 is reproduced exactly by the min-w-0 removal, which is what the work order's own evidence and root_cause attribute it to ('removing min-w-0 from the nav moves scrollWidth to exactly 548'). The comment at lines 337-339 says shrink-0 on the name link 'is the class whose accidental addition reproduces the 548px horizontal overflow QA measured'. Confirmed the guard bites: injecting shrink-0 makes the suite fail at ui.test.tsx:340, so nothing is left unguarded — but a future maintainer reproducing the comment gets 579 and may conclude the guard or measurement is broken.

Fix: Reword the comment to state what was measured: shrink-0 on the name link reproduces a horizontal overflow of the same shape but a different magnitude (579px), and it is the min-w-0 removal that reproduces QA's 548px exactly. Either attribution keeps the assertion; the comment should name both numbers rather than one.

review.title: The new explanatory comment at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:315 adds two more dead Tailwind rules to the production stylesheet. Tailwind scans this test file's comment text, so naming max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and max-w-[var(--x)] in prose emits both as live CSS that no element carries.
review.detail:
The new explanatory comment at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:315 adds two more dead Tailwind rules to the production stylesheet. Tailwind scans this test file's comment text, so naming max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and max-w-[var(--x)] in prose emits both as live CSS that no element carries.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:315`

Evidence: Built CSS (.next/static/chunks/*.css, 16246 bytes, built with TABS_ENV=local and work-order.json moved out of the repo root so its own text could not be the source) contains `.max-w-\[calc\(100\%-2rem\)\]{max-width:calc(100% - 2rem)}` (58 bytes) and `.max-w-\[var\(--x\)\]{max-width:var(--x)}` (41 bytes), both generated from the comment at line 315 and matched by no element in src/. `git show main:tests/components/ui.test.tsx` names only `max-w-[120px]`, so main emits one such dead rule and this PR raises it to three. The work order discloses the pre-existing 120px rule as a known, deliberately-accepted cost but does not account for the two this change adds.

Fix: Either accept and disclose it as the work order does for the 120px rule — one line in risks stating the count goes from one to three — or name the two spellings in prose without the exact token form, so Tailwind's scanner does not read them as class candidates.

review.title: The comment explaining the widened guard quotes max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and max-w-[var(--x)] as literal class strings, and Tailwind 4's scanner reads this test file's comment text like any source file — adding two rules to the shipped stylesheet that no element in src/ carries. main already emits one such dead rule and the work order accepts that cost; this doubles it without disclosure.
review.detail:
The comment explaining the widened guard quotes max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and max-w-[var(--x)] as literal class strings, and Tailwind 4's scanner reads this test file's comment text like any source file — adding two rules to the shipped stylesheet that no element in src/ carries. main already emits one such dead rule and the work order accepts that cost; this doubles it without disclosure.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:315`

Evidence: Built globals.css through @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 from the repo root, PR and main test file, with work-order.json and review/ moved out first (both are scanned and quote the same tokens, which masks the result entirely). Isolated PR: 19856 bytes, includes .max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] and .max-w-[var(--x)]. Isolated main: 19729 bytes, no such rules. Diff is exactly those two rules, 127 bytes. grep confirms src/ uses only max-w-[360px] and max-w-[720px].

Fix: Either add a risks line noting the dead-rule count goes from one to three and is still accepted, or describe the two spellings rather than quoting the exact token form (e.g. 'where the width is a CSS variable or a calc() rather than a literal'). The second costs the scanner nothing.

review.title: The new comment asserts 'Every arbitrary-value Tailwind max-width carries that bracket.' Tailwind 4.3.3 also accepts the unbracketed CSS-variable shorthand max-w-(--cap), which it compiles to a real rule, so the claim justifying the guard's completeness is false for the pinned version. A ceiling written that way reintroduces BUG-4 uncaught. The work order discloses this in residual_risks; the disclosure never reached the comment.
review.detail:
The new comment asserts 'Every arbitrary-value Tailwind max-width carries that bracket.' Tailwind 4.3.3 also accepts the unbracketed CSS-variable shorthand max-w-(--cap), which it compiles to a real rule, so the claim justifying the guard's completeness is false for the pinned version. A ceiling written that way reintroduces BUG-4 uncaught. The work order discloses this in residual_risks; the disclosure never reached the comment.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:313`

Evidence: Both regexes over every spelling named: max-w-[9rem] old=true new=true; max-w-[120px] old=true new=true; max-w-[--cap], [calc(100%-2rem)], [var(--x)], [theme(cap)] old=false new=true; max-w-(--cap) old=false new=false. Dropping the lone string 'max-w-(--cap)' into the repo root produced .max-w-\(--cap\) { max-width: var(--cap) } in a fresh build, so the gap is real and not theoretical. Scale utilities (max-w-xs, max-w-3xl) are also uncaught, which is correct.

Fix: Soften to 'Every bracketed arbitrary-value max-width carries that bracket', and either widen to /max-w-[-[(]/ or note in the comment that Tailwind 4's unbracketed shorthand is deliberately outside the net. The work order judged widening to exceed the review's sanction; recording the limit is cheaper.

review.title: The two new landmark assertions query the whole document rather than the container render() returns, so they depend on every other test in the file having cleaned up. cleanup is explicitly registered and vitest.config.ts does not enable globals, so it is correct today (7 files / 86 tests green) — but this is the one assertion here that future unrelated leakage would silently widen rather than fail loudly, and the file already scopes to the container elsewhere.
review.detail:
The two new landmark assertions query the whole document rather than the container render() returns, so they depend on every other test in the file having cleaned up. cleanup is explicitly registered and vitest.config.ts does not enable globals, so it is correct today (7 files / 86 tests green) — but this is the one assertion here that future unrelated leakage would silently widen rather than fail loudly, and the file already scopes to the container elsewhere.

`tests/components/ui.test.tsx:301`

Evidence: ui.test.tsx:32 registers afterEach(cleanup); vitest.config.ts sets no `globals`, so that hook is load-bearing. Lines 113 and 174 already scope to a container (container.innerHTML, loading.container.innerHTML). Separately confirmed the fixture fix is real: with <main /> as the Shell child the composition yields querySelectorAll('main').length 2 and 'main main'.length 1; with <div /> it yields 1 and 0, and a console.error spy recorded zero calls, so the comment's claim that React is silent about main-in-main is accurate.

Fix: Capture const { container } = render(...) and assert against container.querySelectorAll('main'), matching lines 113 and 174. A robustness nicety, not a defect — the branch is correct as it stands.
